ANA.name: Anaheim Ducks
text: The Ducks are 12-14-1 so far.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
Night to night, they crash the net for second chances and pounce on turnovers.
Their goaltending has let them down.

BOS.name: Boston Bruins
text: The Bruins are 15-9-1 so far.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in 15 of their 25 games.
Night to night, they leave most of the shooting to the forwards and sit back rather than forecheck.
Their goaltending has been stealing games.

BUF.name: Buffalo Sabres
text: The Sabres are 11-11-4 so far.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Their game? They rarely get stuck out on long shifts and rarely block shots.

CGY.name: Calgary Flames
text: The rebuild grinds on in Calgary: no playoffs in four seasons, and a 11-14-2 start.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Night to night, they fire from everywhere, though a lot of it is hopeful and get caught after turnovers too often.
Their power play has no bite and they spend a lot of time in the box.

CAR.name: Carolina Hurricanes
text: The defending champs are picking up right where they left off, 19-3-3 out of the gate, winners of three straight.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in 21 of their 25 games.
Expect them to spend most of the night in the other team’s end and give up dangerous chances.
They create chances even when shorthanded and their penalty kill is airtight.

CHI.name: Chicago Blackhawks
text: The rebuild grinds on in Chicago: no playoffs in six seasons, and a 10-14-2 start, winners of four straight.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Their game? They spend a lot of the night in their own end and find a way to get their shots past the blockers.
Their power play has no bite and they spend a lot of time in the box.

COL.name: Colorado Avalanche
text: Same old Avalanche: 15-7-3, and in the mix again, winners of three straight.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they shoot from distance and play fast, wide-open games.
They stay out of the box.

CBJ.name: Columbus Blue Jackets
text: The rebuild grinds on in Columbus: no playoffs in six seasons, and a 9-14-1 start, losers of three straight.
They’ve played better than that, though, so a bit of luck could turn it around.
On the ice, they send their defensemen in to shoot and shoot from distance.

DAL.name: Dallas Stars
text: The Stars are 15-8-2, which is what we’ve come to expect.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
On the ice, they get a lot of their shots blocked and get in front of a lot of shots.
Their power play is lethal and their penalty kill is airtight.

DET.name: Detroit Red Wings
text: The Red Wings are 10-12-3, still looking for their first playoff spot in ten seasons.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they get in front of a lot of shots and leave most of the shooting to the forwards.

EDM.name: Edmonton Oilers
text: The Oilers are 17-7-4, which is what we’ve come to expect, losers of five straight.
Don’t get too comfortable, though: they’ve been outchanced in most of those games, and that tends to catch up with a team.
Night to night, they lean hard on their top players and settle for a lot of hopeful shots.
Their power play is lethal.

FLA.name: Florida Panthers
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Panthers have bounced back to 15-8-3, winners of three straight.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they rarely block shots and hound the puck in the other team’s end.
Their power play is lethal and their penalty kill is airtight.

LAK.name: Los Angeles Kings
text: The Kings have made the playoffs five years running, but they’re 9-12-2 this time.
They’ve played better than that, though, so a bit of luck could turn it around.
Expect them to leave most of the shooting to the forwards and keep the other team to hopeful shots.

MIN.name: Minnesota Wild
text: The Wild are 18-4-6 so far.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in 15 of their 28 games.
Night to night, they get pinned in their own end on long shifts and get in front of a lot of shots.
They stay out of the box and their goaltending has been stealing games.

MTL.name: Montréal Canadiens
text: The Canadiens are 14-8-4 so far, losers of three straight.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
On the ice, they get into a lot of chippy games and give up dangerous chances.
They spend a lot of time in the box, but their goaltending has been stealing games.

NSH.name: Nashville Predators
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Predators have bounced back to 13-6-6.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they keep things calm after the whistle and let the other team shoot a lot.

NJD.name: New Jersey Devils
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Devils have bounced back to 18-8-0, winners of three straight.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in 19 of their 26 games.
Night to night, they play a finesse game and spend most of the night in the other team’s end.
They stay out of the box and their power play is lethal.

NYI.name: New York Islanders
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Islanders are 12-8-5.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they send their defensemen in to shoot and roll all four lines.
Their goaltending has been stealing games, but their power play has no bite.

NYR.name: New York Rangers
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Rangers are 13-11-1, losers of three straight.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they get right to the net and get a lot of their shots blocked.

OTT.name: Ottawa Senators
text: The Senators are 17-7-3 so far.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in 19 of their 27 games.
Night to night, they rarely get burned after losing the puck and rarely get stuck out on long shifts.

PHI.name: Philadelphia Flyers
text: The Flyers are 10-12-6 so far.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
Their game? They pounce on turnovers and grind games down.

PIT.name: Pittsburgh Penguins
text: The Penguins are 8-15-2 so far.
They’ve played better than that, though, so a bit of luck could turn it around.
Their game? They get right to the net and sit back rather than forecheck.
Their power play has no bite.

SJS.name: San Jose Sharks
text: The Sharks are 12-14-2, still looking for their first playoff spot in seven seasons.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
Their game? They ice the puck a lot to get out of trouble and hit everything that moves.
Their penalty kill leaks and their power play has no bite.

SEA.name: Seattle Kraken
text: The Kraken are 12-10-1, still looking for their first playoff spot in three seasons.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
Expect them to let the other team shoot, but mostly hopeful shots and ice the puck a lot to get out of trouble.
Their penalty kill leaks.

STL.name: St. Louis Blues
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Blues are 14-9-3.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they get to the dangerous chances and keep things calm after the whistle.

TBL.name: Tampa Bay Lightning
text: Same old Lightning: 15-8-2, and in the mix again, losers of three straight.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in 18 of their 25 games.
Expect them to spend most of the night in the other team’s end and rarely block shots.
They stay out of the box.

TOR.name: Toronto Maple Leafs
text: Last season was one to forget in Toronto, and this one hasn’t started much better: they’re 10-14-3.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
On the ice, they find a way to get their shots past the blockers and settle for a lot of hopeful shots.
Their goaltending has let them down and they spend a lot of time in the box.

UTA.name: Utah Mammoth
text: The Mammoth are 14-10-3 so far.
They’ve played better than that record, too, winning the battle for chances more often than not.
Their game? They rarely get stuck out on long shifts and collapse around the net and give up the point.
Their goaltending has let them down.

VAN.name: Vancouver Canucks
text: Last season was one to forget in Vancouver, and this one hasn’t started much better: they’re 6-21-1, losers of three straight.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Expect them to spend a lot of the night in their own end and crash the net for second chances.
Their penalty kill leaks and their goaltending has let them down.

VGK.name: Vegas Golden Knights
text: Last spring’s runners-up look hungry: they’re 15-7-5.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Expect them to get in front of a lot of shots and find a way to get their shots past the blockers.
They stay out of the box and their penalty kill is airtight.

WSH.name: Washington Capitals
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Capitals are 11-12-0.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Their game? They get caught after turnovers too often and get to the dangerous chances.

WPG.name: Winnipeg Jets
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Jets are 14-9-4, winners of three straight.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they find a way to get their shots past the blockers and rarely get burned after losing the puck.
They create chances even when shorthanded, but their penalty kill leaks.
